newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Mexico's Bufete falls in NY.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Mexico's Bufete falls in NY.

text.p: Shares in Mexican construction company Bufete Industrial dropped on Friday, highlighting trade in foreign shares and American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Trade in most Latin American shares was cautious as regional markets kept an eye on the sliding Dow industrials, traders said.
"Nobody's worried about yesterday (when the Dow industrials closed down 94 points), but they are watching New York," a trader said.

Franco-Italian chipmaker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV fell 1-3/4 to 67. The decline came after the French and Italian industry ministers agreed their countries would keep a stake in the company. A source later told Reuters that France and Italy would reduce their 70-percent stake and keep a joint majority stake.
Decliners led advancers by a margin of 330 to 164 among 807 ADRs. Volume in late morning was 38 million shares.

Bufete fell 1-1/4 to 22 in heavy trade after it failed to win a contract to build a thermoelectric plant in Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula. The contract, worth up to $500 million, was won by the United State's AES Corp, Japan's Nichimen Corp and Mexico's Grupo Hermes.
Among other Latin American shares, Telefonos de Mexico TMXI.MX was off 3/8 to 37 and Brazil's Telebras was down 3/4 to 85.
KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV was up 1-5/8 to 29-3/8 after Merrill Lynch raised its rating for the carrier to near- and long-term buy from accumulate.
